title: Clarify that a pronoun with one accessible referent can stay
instruction: Keep an ordinary pronoun when its referent is unambiguous in the supplied context. Name the referent only when readers could reasonably select different antecedents; do not guess it from absent evidence.
scope: Reference checks in scientific prose. This candidate illustrates a possible clarification to B1, subject to overlap review; it is not an accepted new requirement.
rationale: A worked keep case can help prevent unnecessary repetition while preserving the existing ambiguity check.

sources.reference: Toolkit demonstration, not a real expert correction or report.

examples.original: We compared the model with a baseline. It underestimated travel time.
examples.proposed: We compared the model with a baseline. The model underestimated travel time.
examples.context: In this synthetic scenario, the author has confirmed that the model, rather than the baseline, underestimated travel time.
examples.reason: Name the intended referent using the supplied clarification; without that clarification ask the author instead.

counterexamples.text: We fitted a model. It predicts travel time.
counterexamples.context: Only the model is an accessible referent in the supplied context.
counterexamples.why_keep: The pronoun is clear; replacing it with the noun adds no needed disambiguation.

overlap_review.summary: Demonstration only. Read B1 and the no-change guidance, and check upstream before deciding whether an extra example has value or is already covered.

comparisons.reason: B1 already targets ambiguous reference; this may be redundant or useful only as calibration. No novelty claim has been made.
